Preserve logo-first trust treatment as the dominant proof block.
Use the 3-column feature-card system for 5- and 6-item grids, collapsing to single column on mobile.
Keep the gallery as a distinct video-focused section; use reusable video cards rather than custom one-off tiles.

heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro for premium image and video creation.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-width dark creative-studio hero with no single static hero image; instead build an experimental layered composition of CSS-rendered floating output frames, prompt chips, and orb accents. Keep the headline large and dramatic, with the CTA in Techjockey orange. This should feel premium and production-grade, with the media proof deferred to a later video gallery section and logo-proof band.

repetitionBreakers: Logo marquee immediately after hero for trust-first momentum
Tabs-with-preview for Seedream 4.5 to avoid static feature stacking
Alternating dark/light product blocks between Seedream and Seedance
Carousel testimonials instead of a grid to change pace
Highlighted pricing cards followed by a direct final CTA band
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Images & Videos by ByteDance
blueprint.metaDescription: Generate high-quality AI images and videos with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro. Explore image generation, video generation, trusted logos, and a clear path to get started.

sections.backgroundTreatment: dark split hero with floating-orb accents, layered output frames, and subtle orange glow behind the primary CTA
sections.designNote: Make this the highest visual-dominance section. Content-first hero on the left answers: what it is, who it is for, and what to do next. Use the headline as the main conversion anchor, the subheadline to specify creative teams, and a single solid orange Get started CTA in full width on mobile. Right side should show a premium montage of AI image and video outputs, prompt chips, and a cinematic timeline strip. Keep copy continuity with the ad message and avoid secondary CTA clutter.

Place logos early and make them prominent. Use 3-6 recognizable brand logos in a horizontal marquee band to establish credibility fast. If logo count is insufficient, fall back to a compact metric strip. Keep the band dark to contrast with the hero and increase perceived premium value.

Use alternating product blocks because there are multiple product sections and each deserves a distinct story. For Seedream 4.5, use a tabs-with-preview pattern with a live mock preview on the right and tabs on the left to handle the five features without a static card grid. Spotlight the click-driving features first: text–image alignment, high-resolution output, typographic rendering, and multi-image composition. For Seedance 1.5 Pro, switch the rhythm to a darker split-panel list with a cinematic preview area and a compact feature column; highlight audio-video synchronization and cinematic camera control as the strongest differentiators. This section should feel more immersive than the hero and clearly different from the trust band.

Include only if content is available; otherwise keep this section lightweight or omit in production. If shown, use a concise icon-list or 2x2 card grid focused on buying confidence, implementation support, and evaluation ease. Since the current input has no points, keep the visual density low and avoid competing with the product story.

Use centered highlighted pricing cards with strong contrast and one dominant Get started CTA per card. Keep the pricing section conversion-led but not aggressive; it should feel like a decision checkpoint rather than a hard sell. Emphasize the two distinct offers and surface the image product and video product separately. Maintain orange CTA at full opacity, no outlines, no gray states.

With 5 testimonials, use a carousel rather than a grid. Make this section darker to break the page rhythm again and reinforce proof through quotes from creative roles. Prioritize the strongest outcome language: speed, synchronized audio-video, and precision editing. Keep the slides visually editorial and compact.

Use a centered floating card as the final conversion moment. Since the product already has strong proof and a pricing checkpoint, the closing section should be clean, direct, and low-friction. Keep the CTA as Get started only, with full-width mobile treatment and no alternate button text. Make this the final action path after the proof-led sequence.

Optional end-cap band for press or logo reinforcement if assets exist; otherwise replace with a final CTA banner. Use a horizontal logo strip or short marquee to close with credibility rather than extra explanation. Keep this visually lighter than the testimonial block so the page ends with momentum.

blueprint.designPersonality: Confident, editorial, and production-minded. Feels like a high-end creative tool for teams that care about craft, speed, and control. Dark, polished, interactive, and visually intelligent without drifting into generic purple AI branding.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a premium dark creative studio aesthetic with layered product renders, floating prompt chips, thumbnail strips, and a gallery section containing embedded video previews. Logos should be the primary proof signal in a marquee band near the top, followed by compact trust stats. If product UI assets are limited, build rich CSS-based shells showing generated frames, timeline strips, and prompt-to-output transformations.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The headline is long and feature-rich, so it needs a smaller high-impact size to avoid breaking the hero layout while still feeling premium.

colours.colourReason: The brand palette is strictly derived from Techjockey’s provided colors: deep black for the hero background, orange as the primary CTA and action accent, and white/grey for contrast and readability. This keeps the page distinct, premium, and fully brand-compliant without introducing any unapproved colors.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Split hero with brand logo, large headline, supporting paragraph, and a short bullet-value list; strong above-the-fold hierarchy with one dominant message and minimal CTA emphasis.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Single-column hero followed by conversion form card, then stacked content sections; limited modular depth with clear separation between headline blocks and detail blocks.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Solid white form/content card with simple rectangular structure, subtle border/shadow treatment, compact interior spacing, and no glassmorphism or decorative effects.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion is form-led rather than button-led; use one dominant action near the hero/form area and keep secondary actions absent or understated.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No pricing pattern present in the reference layout.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer not visible in the provided reference; no extractable footer pattern.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Brand/logo media only in hero; no rich product imagery, no video panel, and no interactive media gallery. Visual emphasis is text-first.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Use stacked feature sections with a headline, short descriptive paragraph, and bullet or list-based capability breakdown; suitable for long-form B2B detail pages and progressive disclosure through sectioning rather than tabs.
referenceMap.formPattern: Lead capture form card placed directly below hero; dense field grouping with hidden tracking inputs and a conversion-oriented title. Pattern favors immediate qualification over exploratory browsing.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static presentation with no visible motion system; interaction is primarily form submission and optional carousel code comments not active in the rendered layout.
componentPatterns: Hero banner with logo + headline + bullets
Optional carousel scaffold in markup, but not active in the visible pattern
designNotes: Prioritize B2B conversion with a direct, utility-first message.
Keep navigation and decorative elements minimal; the layout is content-dense but structurally simple.
Use high-contrast section bands to separate acquisition and detail content.
This reference is better suited to a product landing page with embedded lead gen than a marketing story page with rich interaction.

mustHaveMoments: Dark-theme hero with a strong product/value statement and one primary CTA
Prominent logo-first trust band near the top, before deep product explanation
Video gallery section with motion-led previews to showcase Seedance capabilities
Stacked feature sections for Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro with clear capability breakdowns
Pricing or quote section framed as an evaluation step, not a checkout step
Testimonials from creative roles to reinforce professional relevance
Final conversion block with demo/quote CTA and concise reassurance
avoidPatterns: Do not use a light, airy editorial style that weakens the premium AI positioning
Do not lead with pricing as the first or most prominent decision element
Do not overload the page with too many competing CTAs
Do not rely on badges alone for trust; logos must be the dominant signal
Do not use decorative or glassmorphism-heavy UI that reduces perceived enterprise seriousness
Do not make the gallery static-only; it should visibly showcase video motion
designStrategy.reasoning: This page is for professionals evaluating advanced AI image and video generation, so the strongest strategy is lead-generation with a solution-aware, product-led narrative. The visitor likely understands the category but needs proof of quality, capability, and enterprise readiness. Because the instruction specifies that logos are the primary trust signal, trust should be built first through recognizable logos or a logo wall rather than generic badges or stats. The dark theme supports a premium, cutting-edge AI feel and helps video/gallery content stand out. A split hero is the best fit because it can balance messaging on one side with a visual or motion panel on the other, while keeping the main CTA prominent but not overly aggressive. Balanced section density suits the long content volume and professional audience: enough detail to evaluate, but not so dense that it feels technical or cluttered. The gallery section with videos is essential because Seedance is video-generation focused and motion proof is the most persuasive demonstration of quality.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
